headline: Turin ATP Finals: Carlos Alcaraz sweeps Alexander Zverev 6-2, 7-6 to lift maiden crown
whyCareReason: Alcaraz captures his maiden Nitto ATP Finals trophy with a 14-match winning streak, joining Agassi, Federer, and Djokovic as Career Super Slam winners.
teaser: Carlos Alcaraz completes a flawless 5-0 week in Turin, saving three set points in the second-set tiebreak to defeat World No. 1 Alexander Zverev 6-2, 7-6(7).
story:
Carlos Alcaraz etched his name into tennis history on Sunday, 22 November, producing an indoor hard-court masterclass to defeat World No. 1 Alexander Zverev 6-2, 7-6(7) at Inalpi Arena in Turin.

Having rallied past Ben Shelton 3-6, 6-3, 7-6(1) in Saturday semifinals while Zverev eliminated Daniil Medvedev 7-6(0), 6-4, the championship clash pitted the two sharpest servers in the draw. Alcaraz struck twice to breeze through the opening set before saving three set points in a breathtaking second-set tiebreak (9-7).

The triumph capped an undefeated 5-0 campaign worth $5,171,000 and marked the 23-year-old Spaniard 14th consecutive match win. Joining Andre Agassi, Roger Federer, and Novak Djokovic, Alcaraz became only the fourth man ever to win all four Grand Slam titles plus the year-end championship.
stakes: Undefeated champion Alcaraz pockets the maximum $5,171,000 payout from the $15,750,000 prize pool and secures 1,500 ranking points.
rivalryAngle: World No. 2 Alcaraz outlasted World No. 1 Zverev after surviving Ben Shelton in a three-set semifinal.
funFacts: Alcaraz completed a perfect 5-0 undefeated week to claim the maximum $5,171,000 champion payout.
At age 23, he became the fourth man in history to own all four Grand Slams and the ATP Finals crown.
French debutants Theo Arribage and Albano Olivetti lifted the doubles trophy 3-6, 7-6(2), [10-6] over Arevalo and Pavic.
